subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix after exact-head runtime and RSS proof is supplied?
rationale: The implementation is a plausible focused repair, but it changes compatibility-sensitive prompt/session inputs and event-loop scheduling, so automation cannot safely accept the upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Prove Final Head, Then Land
options.body: Require a comparable exact-head embedded-run benchmark with event-loop latency, total duration, peak RSS, and resulting bootstrap matches before accepting the compatibility risk.

options.title: Accept Current Focused Proof
options.body: Land after checks are refreshed while explicitly accepting that uncommon glob and scheduling behavior is supported primarily by focused tests and loader-level proof.

options.title: Pause For Broader Design
options.body: Keep or close the PR in favor of worker isolation, caching, or priority scheduling if maintainers do not want to own a custom glob implementation.

recommendation.title: Prove Final Head, Then Land
recommendation.body: Require a comparable exact-head embedded-run benchmark with event-loop latency, total duration, peak RSS, and resulting bootstrap matches before accepting the compatibility risk.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature history spans the bootstrap reader, internal hooks, and the session-context boundaries that require the decision.
